text: The Patriots' turnover differential woes—one of Mike Vrabel's four identity pillars—came back to haunt them in a 30-24 Thursday night loss to the Bears in Chicago, with Caleb Williams outdueling Drake Maye and throwing two touchdown passes in what amounted to Round 2 of their matchup. Film breakdowns of Maye's performance and the Patriots defense reveal the areas where execution broke down, though there were some bright spots amid the loss: Rhamondre Stevenson reached a career high in receiving yards and continues to do the little things right while approaching 100 carries for the sixth straight season, suggesting the Patriots' offensive weapons aren't entirely the problem. Beat writers have catalogued eight key takeaways from the loss and pulled postgame comments from Mike Vrabel and his players, all pointing to a team that knows exactly what went wrong but now faces the challenge of correcting turnover habits if they want to climb back into contention. The film doesn't lie, and neither do the statistics—but the turnover battle, more than any other factor, appears to be the fundamental issue separating the Patriots from the success Vrabel's system demands.
